config.title: Dominion rl-v3: Chain

goal.label: Head to head vs rl-v1's champion

config.goal_text: the best Dominion model yet: at least 55% head to head against rl-v1's champion (net 2,200), without dropping below its 82.8% against the GA base

series.label: vs rl-v1's champion (200 eval games, head to head)
value vs final result on fresh games (1.0 = no idea)

runs.note: PPO from rl-v1's best checkpoint (iteration 2,219) with rl-v2's helper inputs added at zero weight. The evaluation games are only measured, never trained on.

decisions.title: Card school for cards the champion never tried
decisions.text: The card audit: Chapel never bought, Mine/Library/Moneylender bought in 4% of games, Council Room/Smithy/Village/Merchant 10-16%. In 15% of training games (stages 2-3) the learner's first buys are forced to 2 copies of one of 10 such cards, not recorded, so it learns to play them while buying stays its own choice.
decisions.rejected: Recording the forced buys (wrong PPO ratios); a starting deck with the card (changes the rules).

decisions.title: Curriculum ends against the champion
decisions.text: Stage 1 rl-v1's own league (gate 84% vs GA), stage 2 + the frozen champion as 25% of games (gate 56% vs it), stage 3 open league with rl-v2 too. rl-v1 learned to beat az-v1 only once az-v1 was in its league.

decisions.title: Start from rl-v1's checkpoint, widened with the helper inputs
decisions.text: rl-v1 r2 was still improving when it stopped (67% to 81% vs GA over 2,200 iterations), and the helper inputs lifted rl-v2 by 3 points. Weights and Adam state loaded; new inputs at zero weight.
decisions.rejected: From zero (rl-v2 plateaued at ~74%); imitation of the GA (rl-v1 already did that).

decisions.title: No chain module in the player
decisions.text: The released player is the network alone. On the chain exam rl-v1's champion picks the coin-best action 91.6% of the time, but with a turn planner (value judge or coins judge, K=32) or a chain rule choosing its actions it scored 48.8%, 48.5%, 48.2% (engine kingdoms) and 49.9% head to head against itself without it.
decisions.rejected: A statistical turn planner at play time (no gain, 20x slower); a hand-written chain rule (changed 15 of 6,335 decisions).
